description: Make the deterministic plan-runner authoritative over which issue is planned: thread the selectIssueFn-chosen issue id into the planner prompt and have the subagent-planner obey it (never re-select top-of-queue).

userStories.title: Thread the selected issue id into the planner task prompt (runner authoritative)
userStories.description: As the cam sidecar, I need runPlanPhase to build a target-aware planner task prompt from the issue that selectIssueFn chose, so the spawned planner plans that exact issue instead of self-selecting top-of-queue, and PRD.issueNumber comes out correct.
acceptanceCriteria: runPlanPhase builds the planner task prompt from the issue returned by selectIssueFn() (its .id) AFTER the null-check, and threads that prompt into the planner spawn (resolveAndSpawnPlanner -> buildPlannerWorkerArgv) instead of the target-blind DEFAULT_PLANNER_TASK_PROMPT. [oracle: bun test + grep -qE 'issue\.id|selectedIssue|targetId|buildPlannerTaskPrompt' src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts]

The built planner task prompt names the exact issue id and instructs the planner not to re-select from the backlog (e.g. 'Plan issue CAM-157 specifically ... do not re-select'). A unit test asserts the built prompt contains the selected issue id and a do-not-re-select phrase. [oracle: bun test]
The opts.plannerTaskPrompt override seam is still honored when explicitly provided (backward compat for existing tests that inject a fixed prompt). [oracle: bun test]

E2E regression (the guard unit tests missed): drive runPlanPhase against a REAL tmux pane on a private socket (test.skipIf when tmux absent) with selectIssueFn returning an issue that is NOT top-of-queue, using a planner stub that reads the pane's task prompt and echoes the named issue's numeric id into scripts/cam/prd.json; assert the resulting prd.json.issueNumber === the target's numeric id (157-style), never the top-of-queue issue. [oracle: bun test test/integration/plan-runner-target-obey.test.ts]

Bare selection path unchanged: when selectIssueFn returns the top-of-queue issue (no explicit target), the runner threads THAT issue's id into the prompt and the e2e stub yields prd.json.issueNumber === that issue with no null issueNumber. [oracle: bun test]
When selectIssueFn returns null, no planner is spawned and runPlanPhase returns { kind: 'no-plannable-issue' } (halt unchanged). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: ROOT CAUSE: src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts ~486 resolves plannerTaskPrompt = opts.plannerTaskPrompt ?? DEFAULT_PLANNER_TASK_PROMPT BEFORE the issue is selected (~505), then discards the selected `issue` (only null-checked) and spawns with the generic prompt at ~518. Move prompt-building AFTER selection: build a target-aware prompt from issue.id (add a small pure helper, e.g. buildPlannerTaskPrompt(issueId), exported for unit testing), preserving the opts.plannerTaskPrompt override. Numeric id derivation can reuse the split('-').at(-1) pattern from src/issues/select.ts numericIdSuffix. E2E pattern: mirror test/integration/plan-runner-no-prd.test.ts and plan-runner-pane-spawn.test.ts (private socket swapSocketSpawn, respawn-pane stub, real isPaneAlive, no-op sleepFn) but the stub must WRITE scripts/cam/prd.json echoing the id parsed from the prompt so the runner->prompt->prd.json chain is exercised end-to-end (the missing gate: existing unit tests mocked selectIssueFn and never drove the planner-obeys path; fakes-mentem class). ship-finalize.ts reads `typeof prd.issueNumber === 'number'`, so issueNumber must be numeric. Do NOT reintroduce claude -p (CAM-42) or a --permission-mode CLI flag. Read scripts/cam/patterns.md (spawnSync exit-status guard, real-git/real-tmux integration test pattern) before coding.

userStories.title: subagent-planner honors an explicit target issue id (both copies + re-embed)
userStories.description: As the cam planner subagent, I need to obey an explicit target issue id named in my task prompt so I plan exactly that issue and set PRD.issueNumber to its numeric id, never self-selecting top-of-queue when a target is provided.
acceptanceCriteria: .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md instructs the planner: when the task prompt names a specific target issue id, plan EXACTLY that issue (read scripts/cam/issues/<prefix>-<N-padded>.json), set PRD.issueNumber to its numeric id, and do NOT self-select or re-order from the backlog. [oracle: grep -qiE 'plan (exactly|that) (issue|the named)|do not re-select|target issue id' .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md]

templates/agents/subagent-planner.md carries the equivalent target-honoring instruction (generic downstream wording; the two copies intentionally diverge, cam dual-copy is per-file). [oracle: grep -qiE 'target issue|do not re-select|plan (exactly|that)' templates/agents/subagent-planner.md]
The embedded copy is regenerated (bun run embed-vendor) so src/vendor/_generated.ts matches templates/, and embed-vendor:check passes. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: TWO copies to edit: .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md (cam-cli runtime, what the sidecar-spawned planner actually reads via --agent subagent-planner) AND templates/agents/subagent-planner.md (downstream cam init source of truth, embedded into src/vendor/_generated.ts). These two files ALREADY DIVERGE (the .claude copy is cam-cli-specific, the templates copy is generic) so diff before editing and do NOT try to make them byte-identical (patterns.md 'cam dual-copy is per-file'). embed-vendor embeds templates/, not .claude/, so only the templates edit requires re-embed; edit both, then run `bun run embed-vendor` and verify with `bun run embed-vendor:check` (self-hosting pattern, patterns.md 'Agent-prompt self-hosting'). Issue file naming: filename is 4-digit zero-padded (CAM-0157.json) but the `id` field inside is unpadded (CAM-157); the prompt from US-001 passes the unpadded id, so the honor-instruction must tell the planner to pad when resolving the file (padStart(4,'0'), per src/issues/backlog.ts:185). issueNumber must be the numeric suffix (157), matching ship-finalize.ts `typeof === 'number'`. No em-dash in the .md prose that is human-facing; agent-instruction files may use em-dash/emoji freely (global CLAUDE.md exception).
